chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Usama from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Umar stood on the pulpit and said, 'What do you say, O companions of Muhammad, regarding the divorce of a slave girl?' So no one answered him. Then he said, 'What do you say, O owner of the Ma'afari cloak?' — meaning Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him). So he gestured with his hand, indicating two divorces.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for divorcing a slave girl according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the scholarly authority of Imam Ali (AS) during the caliphate of Umar, where his silent gesture clarified the specific fiqh ruling for divorcing a slave girl (Umm al-Walad). In Shia jurisprudence, this incident is often cited to demonstrate the continuity of prophetic knowledge and the distinct legal status of slave women compared to free women, where two divorces are required to effect a final separation.
